transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith, one of the psychiatrists here. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Well, I’m here because I just keep blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. I've been... snapping on my operations calls at work, and even at my family when I get home. It's getting really bad, and that is just not how I’ve ever handled things before.
When did you first notice this change in your temper, and has it been constant since then or does it come and go?

It's been going on for about three weeks now. It started right after... well, we had a valve failure and an injury down at the facility. Ever since that happened, it's been pretty much constant. I just haven't been able to shake it.
Since the incident happened, have you been having unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the valve failure or the injury that keep intruding into your mind?

Yeah, I have. It's... well, I can just be sitting at the kitchen table, or trying to answer some emails from home, and suddenly I’m right back there. I see the flash from that valve, and the smoke in the aisle. It's like it just shoves everything else out of my head.
Have you noticed yourself going out of your way to avoid certain places, tasks, or conversations at work that remind you of the valve failure and injury?

No, not really. I mean, I still have to do my job, so I can't just avoid things. I haven't noticed myself staying away from any specific places or tasks, and I still talk to the same people. I just get angry when I do.
Since the incident, have you noticed times when you feel detached from yourself or your surroundings, like things aren't quite real, or gaps in your memory of the event?

I don't know about feeling like things aren't real, I haven't really noticed that. But the memory gaps... yeah, I definitely have those. 

What really scares me is that there are just chunks of it I can’t pull up. Especially those seconds right around the alarm going off and the shutdown. I mean, people at the facility keep telling me I did the right things, but... I just have a blank spot there. I can't remember actually doing it.
Since the incident, have you noticed feeling unusually jumpy or easily startled, constantly on guard, or having trouble falling or staying asleep?

Yeah, sleep has been... it's been really tough. Most nights I just lie there in bed, and I can hear that alarm going off in my head. And when I finally do manage to doze off, I end up waking up sweating. I keep having these dreams about the smoke, and hearing people yelling. So by the time morning rolls around, I feel like I never even slept at all.
Would you say these symptoms have made it hard for you to function normally at work or at home—like missing work, conflict with family, or trouble completing daily tasks?

Yeah, it definitely has. I haven't even been cleared to go back to the plant yet, so I'm just trying to work from home. But even doing that... I'm missing things on conference calls, and I'm upsetting people. Honestly, I'm afraid I'm becoming a liability to the team instead of the manager they actually need right now.
It's been about three weeks since the incident—do you think these symptoms are staying the same, getting worse, or starting to ease up as time goes on?

Yeah, it's been right around three weeks. Ever since the... the valve failure and the injury at the facility. Honestly, I wouldn't say it's easing up at all. It's just been going on like this the entire time. It really feels like it's just staying exactly the same as day one.
Since the incident, have you noticed a change in your ability to feel positive emotions—like happiness, love, or satisfaction—even in situations where you normally would?

Yeah, I have. It's... it's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just blank. Like, my wife will make a nice dinner, or my kids will be going on about their soccer games just like normal. And I know I should feel glad, you know? I should feel happy to just be sitting there with them. But it's like... there's just nothing in me that can respond to it anymore.
With everything you've been going through these past few weeks, have you had any thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself or not wanting to be alive?

No, no I haven't had any thoughts like that. I mean, it's been a really tough time, and I feel completely drained... but I don't want to hurt myself. I definitely still want to be here for my wife and kids. I just want to figure out how to get past this and get back to normal, you know?
